issues.failure_explanation: Scaling Lemma a11 (kappa_V(A) <= n 2^n eta^{1-n} for ||A||<=1) to ||A||<=R and using (a27) gives, on the event G and ||A||<=R, max_j kappa(lambda_j)^2 <= kappa_V^2 <= n^2 4^n (R/eta_0)^{2n-2}, whereas the recursion only guarantees tau_K >= eta_0 (3R/eta_0)^n. The comparison needed for F(tau_K), namely n^2 (4/3)^n (R/eta_0)^{n-2} <= 1, fails for every R > eta_0 and n >= 2 (e.g. n=2, R=2 eta_0 gives 64/9 > 1). The implication is in fact false, not merely unjustified: for A = [[0,1],[c,0]] with c=0.0025 one has ||A||=1=R and eta(A)=2 sqrt(c)=0.1=eta_0, but max_j kappa(lambda_j)^2 = (1+c)^2/(4c) ≈ 100.5, while tau_K < 2 eta_0 (3R/eta_0)^2 = 180 and can be made ≈ 95 < 100.5 by choosing tau_0 appropriately. Thus the bootstrap recursion is never legitimately seen to terminate and Proposition a14 is unproven as stated.

failure_location.quote: Then $\tau_K\ge \eta_0(3R/\eta_0)^n$ and so Lemma \ref{a11} combined with (\ref{a27}) implies $G\wedge\magn{A}\le R\implies F(\tau_K)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the termination threshold: take K = ceil(2 n lg(3R/eta_0) + lg(eta_0/tau_0) + 2 lg n + 2n) so that tau_K >= n^2 4^n (R/eta_0)^{2n-2}, and enlarge the bracket in the conclusion accordingly (e.g. [6n lg(3R/eta_0) + 3 lg(2 eta_0/tau_0) + 6 lg n + 6n]). This is a contained reoptimization; the bootstrap statement and all downstream asymptotic claims survive with slightly worse constants.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition a14's complete-bootstrap bound is not established. Theorem a1 (label a1), whose proof invokes Proposition a14, loses this input independently of the Proposition a19 defect (ISSUE-004).
issues.title: Proposition a14: bootstrap termination implication (eta(A)>=eta_0 and ||A||<=R) ==> F(tau_K) is false; the K schedule is too small
issues.why_classification: The recursion itself is valid, but the termination step is a false claimed implication (not a typo), so the K schedule must be re-optimized and the bracket constants re-derived; this is a contained reoptimization with no loss of regime, rate, or advertised scope, hence moderate rather than minor or serious.

issues.failure_explanation: The event ||vec delta odot v||^2 <= 2r^2/s only forces that not all of the large-coefficient entries T = {j : |v_j|^2 >= 2r^2/s} are selected (probability 1 - rho^{|T|}), not that none are selected (probability (1-rho)^{|T|}); the displayed inequality is false (e.g. v = (r sqrt(2/s), 0, ..., 0) with rho = 1/2 gives LHS 1 but RHS 1/2). The correct estimate yields #T <= ln(1/(1-s/2))/ln(1/rho), which is smaller than the claimed log(2/s)/rho in the regimes used, so the lemma's conclusion survives; the same invalid inequality recurs in a load-bearing way in Lemma a18 (ISSUE-003).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace (1-rho)^{|T|} by 1 - rho^{|T|} (equivalently, bound the event by Pr(Binom(|T|,rho) <= |T|-1)) and conclude #T <= ln(1/(1-s/2))/ln(1/rho) <= log(2/s)/rho; a short local fix leaving the stated conclusion unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma a17's proof is invalid as written, but its conclusion is preserved (indeed strengthened) by the corrected bound, so no labelled result loses an established input; Lemma a18 applies only a17's surviving conclusion and is treated in ISSUE-003.
issues.title: Lemma a17: small-ball bound Pr(||delta*v||^2 <= 2r^2/s) <= (1-rho)^{|T|} is invalid
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction of the small-ball estimate restores the proof with the same (indeed stronger) conclusion and no change to any downstream guarantee; it is a short, local, routine repair.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \mathcal N_{k, j} = \mathcal N_k \cap \{\tilde v: a_k(\tilde v) = j\}, \quad 1 \le j \le \frac{\log(2/s)}{\rho}.
By combining this with (\ref{a32}), applying union bound over $k, j$, and using the second hypothesis of the lemma we obtain the desired result.

issues.failure_explanation: The estimate Pr(||vec delta odot v-tilde||^2 <= 2r'^2/s) <= (1-rho)^j is invalid (the same error as in Lemma a17): the event forces at most one of the j large entries to be selected, giving (1-rho)^j + j rho (1-rho)^{j-1}, which equals 1 at j=1, so the paper's usable value (1-rho)+rho/2 = 1-rho/2 at j=1 rests on the false inequality. Independently, the relaxation (a32) is vacuous at j=1 (max((1-rho)^0, 1/2)^n = 1) while the entropy bound gives |N_{k,1}| >= 1 (the union over j starts at 1 and log(es/(2 eps^2)) > 0 under the hypotheses), so the union bound over k, j contributes at least 1 from j=1 and cannot yield e^{-n rho/2}. Hence the lemma's conclusion does not follow from the displayed estimates.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Re-derive the per-vector estimate using the full support of v-tilde (e.g. Pr(||vec delta odot v-tilde||^2 <= 2r'^2/s) <= Pr(Binom(#supp(v-tilde),rho) <= 1) with #supp(v-tilde) <= j (log(2/s)/rho)^{1/K}, yielding p(v-tilde,r')^n <= e^{-n rho (#supp(v-tilde)-1)/2}-type bounds) and redo the union-bound bookkeeping, including the j=1 layer and the stated second hypothesis; the lemma's statement is plausibly salvageable by this contained reargument.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma a18's compressible-vector bound with additive error e^{-n rho/2} is unproven; Proposition a19, which unions the bounds of Lemmas a16 and a18, and Theorem a1 lose this input.
issues.title: Lemma a18: per-vector probability estimate uses the invalid (1-rho)^j bound, and the final union bound is vacuous at j=1
issues.why_classification: The per-vector estimate and the final union bound must be reworked (a contained but nontrivial reargument with no new global proof architecture), while the lemma's conclusion is expected to survive; this is more than a typo fix but avoids major loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Because $\alg{Comp}(2\eps\sqrt n,s)\\sqcup\alg{Incomp}(2\eps\sqrt n,s)$ is a partitioning the sphere, the event $\sigma_{n-m}(M+N_g)\le\eps$ is the union of the events whose probabilities are bounded in each of Lemma \ref{a16} and Lemma \ref{a18}. We obtain the final result by a union bound.

issues.failure_explanation: The Incomp/Comp partition forces a single threshold s, and Lemma a18 requires s >= s_min = 2^{3(K+1)} eps^2 n^2 R^{2K}/rho^K; the union bound then gives binom(n,m+1) s_min^{m+1} ≈ (2^{3(K+1)} n^3 R^{2K} eps^2/rho^K)^{m+1}, which exceeds the stated n^{2+m+1} R^{2K(m+1)} eps^{2(m+1)} by the factor 2^{3(K+1)(m+1)} n^{2m}/rho^{K(m+1)}. Matching the stated bound would require rho^K >= 2^{3(K+1)} n^{2-1/(m+1)}, which fails in every regime: for rho = n^{alpha-1} one has rho^K = n^{2-2/alpha} (e.g. rho = n^{-1/2}, K = 4 gives rho^K = n^{-2}), and it fails even at rho = 1 (K = 2). With the correct coefficient, the main proof's m=1 term becomes 2^{6K+2} n^{2-K}/rho^{K-1} >> n^{-K}; since both the m=0 and m=1 terms scale as eta^{2/3}, no choice of eta, lambda, K, or R compensates, so the proofs of both bounds in Theorem a1 collapse in the sparse regime and even at rho = 1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair: fixing Lemma a18 (ISSUE-003) does not close the gap, since the tension between Lemma a16's binom(n,m+1) s^{m+1} and Lemma a18's lower bound s >= 2^{3(K+1)} eps^2 n^2 R^{2K}/rho^K is intrinsic to the compressible/incompressible argument as written, and rebalancing eta, lambda, K, or R cannot compensate (the m=1 term always exceeds n^{-K} by a factor rho^{-(K-1)}). A repair needs a genuinely stronger incompressible-vector estimate or a different least-singular-value argument, i.e. essentially new proof architecture for the paper's main technical proposition.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem a1 (the paper's main result, hence the abstract's polylogarithmic and logarithmic regularization claims) and the spectral-radius algorithm thm:added-1, whose guarantee and runtime rely on Theorem a1, lose their proofs; the advertised sparse-regime bounds are not established.
issues.title: Proposition a19: stated bound is smaller than Lemma a16 permits at the s forced by Lemma a18; the main theorem's proof breaks in the sparse regime
issues.why_classification: Every available resolution requires new proof architecture for the central singular-value proposition and abandons the paper's advertised sparse regime; no parameter reoptimization recovers the main theorem's quantitative bounds, so the issue is serious even though the dense-case conclusions are known from other works.
